notes: Canonical scorer truth. Do not expose to Z-SCOPE analysis context. Version 10 promotes manually verified extra findings from the auto_unified_wsl_structured_20260520_2 run and adds alternate public-wrapper anchors; version 9 refreshes line anchors after public-header and wrapper entry refactors; version 8 adds a high-tier ISSUE41-* suite derived from GitHub issue #41 distributed C/S messaging and task-creation models.

vulnerabilities.title: Task parser trusts payload_length and can read beyond supplied buffer
Internal network handler multiplies unchecked Task binary size before memcpy
vulnerabilities.notes: Valid when the internal Task object is treated as untrusted at this entry. Through the current parser path payload_length is capped by MAX_TASK_SIZE, so reports should ideally mention the entry-scope assumption.

vulnerabilities.title: Attacker-controlled log buffer is used as printf format string
Plugin unregister relocks registry mutex through lookup while already holding it
Cleanup frees temp_buffer twice when resource_a is positive
Network error path leaks error_msg and recovery_buffer
Worker threads increment global shared counter without synchronization
File permission check is separated from fopen use
User command and TASK_ENV are concatenated and passed to system
Thread id array allocated during initialization is never released
Dispatcher cleanup passes TaskConfig to SharedResources cleanup
Network string receive allocates max_len + 1 without overflow check
Shutdown flag g_running is read by workers and written by cleanup without synchronization
Task serialization adds header size to untrusted payload length without overflow check
Control message parser dereferences strchr result without checking for ':'
Cache entry is published to the global list before value initialization completes
Cache lookup returns borrowed value after releasing the lock while remove can free it
Reference count is incremented and decremented after dropping the cache lock
Registered callback context points to a cache entry that can later be removed and freed
Lifecycle callback is invoked while holding the cache mutex
Asynchronous flush thread receives the address of a stack-allocated FlushJob
Config reload returns on allocation failure while still holding g_config_lock
Global config pointer is checked outside the mutex before lazy initialization
Condition variable wait uses if instead of while and decrements pending_jobs after wake
Metrics buffer overwrites the only pointer with realloc result and can leak the old allocation
Negative receive result is cast to size_t and used as memcpy length
Topic formatter writes the NUL terminator one byte past the stack buffer
Status reply sends an only partially initialized stack struct
Config value slice frees a pointer into the middle of the caller buffer
Frame parser uses an attacker-controlled VLA size on the stack
Protocol decoder casts packet + 1 to uint32_t pointer and dereferences it
Connection close does not clear the watched fd before future event dispatch
Rules mapping is unmapped without clearing the global pointer used by later rule matching
Mesh control sessions are registered globally but the disconnect cleanup hook is never initialized
Customize OPEN control messages create global sessions without any transport cleanup path
DETACH control messages unlink a global session without releasing the session allocation
Guarded subscription unregister frees the node without destroying its nested mutex resource
Pipe dispatch and close paths acquire scheduler and control locks in opposite order
Closed pipe node is unlinked with next pointing to itself and can trap later traversal
Self-referential pipe traversal emits an error log on every loop iteration
Timer callback can wait on a pipe control lock held by close while close waits on the scheduler lock
Deleting an OS node frees the primary list node without walking and releasing its ProcNode child list
Policy AVL upsert looks up full strings but inserts only the first 128 bytes of the key
Route registration frees a node after AVL insertion failure without removing stale tree links
Shared counter locking is compiled out on non-64-bit builds while the resource remains shared
Plugin registration overwrites an occupied slot without releasing the previous plugin state
vulnerabilities.notes: Public td_register_plugin documents replacement of an existing name, but the implementation writes the target slot directly and increments count without invoking the old cleanup path or releasing stored context.

vulnerabilities.title: Watched connection descriptor is shared between receiver and public event paths without synchronization
Platform task execution forwards caller-controlled task strings directly to the OS command launcher
vulnerabilities.notes: The platform abstraction is declared in include/platform_impl.h and is discovered as an external scan root when header_files includes *.h.

vulnerabilities.title: Dispatcher readiness flag is read without synchronization while cleanup tears down shared queue state
vulnerabilities.notes: A concurrent submitter can observe stale readiness and continue into queue locking while cleanup has already started destroying dispatcher resources.

vulnerabilities.title: Rules mapping globals are remapped and unmapped without synchronization
vulnerabilities.notes: Multiple public td_configure_rules callers can race while one path remaps or unmaps globals and another path reads them for matching.

vulnerabilities.title: Module cleanup unlinks a node under the registry lock then frees members after releasing the lock
OS node removal frees the parent while child ProcNode-style records remain linked and uncollected
Shared rollback path frees the same payload twice when the second initialization stage fails
Component destroy detaches a node but returns on configuration removal failure before releasing it
System file unregister frees the wrapper node while leaking its dynamically allocated path payload
Activation failure rollback unlinks a globally registered node but drops nested session resources
Reader-channel cleanup ignores the stored role and invokes the creator-only release path
Error logging path allocates a formatted message copy and returns without releasing it
Initialization publishes a registry node before mutex and payload initialization complete
Message decoder casts an unaligned packet offset to uint32_t after only a two-byte length check
Patch unload frees the primary patch node but misses the table-node child allocation
AVL insertion failure is ignored after linking the node, losing ownership and cleanup state
Protocol length calculation trusts a packet unit count and can copy beyond the supplied frame
Offline parser reads record count before validating the expected 64-bit magic value
Resource-table unload releases the table shell without walking nested bucket records
Ready flag is set before the shared node reaches its final initialized state
Patch tree cleanup frees the root record while leaking left and right child records
Peak-stat query allocates a PID statistics buffer and returns copied data without releasing it
Network header receive loop spins on repeated receive failures with no delay or exit path
Secure-channel probe returns a successful status when the receive-based classifier fails
Client cleanup sends a hardcoded role parameter even though the channel role is available
System-call failure leaves local registry state changed instead of restoring the previous value
Allocation failure path returns while still holding the auxiliary lifecycle lock
Reference count is incremented after the lookup lock has been dropped
External callback is invoked while the global registry lock is held
Detached async worker receives the address of a stack-allocated job descriptor
Metrics resize overwrites the only global pointer with the realloc result
Negative receive result is cast to size_t and used as a memcpy length
Closed descriptor remains globally watched and is reused for later receive dispatch
Policy route lookup uses the full key while insertion stores a truncated key
Macro-guarded shared counter update compiles to a no-op lock outside strict builds
Resource-case wrapper casts negative mode values to huge unsigned allocation sizes
vulnerabilities.notes: mode is a signed public API parameter; mode=-2 wraps to UINT32_MAX after mode+1, causing area+1 to wrap in the downstream allocation path before pid_list[0] is written.

vulnerabilities.title: Collection label cache uses a fixed byte limit smaller than the stated element-count specification
C/S protocol receive path trusts the message length after checking only the magic field
Receive retry loop repeats EAGAIN and EINTR forever without timeout or retry budget
Reliable fd with high check bits is passed to a lower-layer interface that expects a raw fd
Protocol mismatch is detected but accepted under default non-strict authentication mode
Multi-step C/S initialization leaks a partition on failure and retry can use an uninitialized tag
Task array expansion updates a global pointer and frees the old array without synchronization
High-version subscriber processes low-version state reports without filtering version zero
Shared listener resource is closed and freed without checking outstanding references
Client write to a closed peer can raise SIGPIPE because the C/S send path never masks the signal
Work fd attribute setup passes raw fd indexes to validation code that expects encoded fds

excluded_vulnerabilities.former_title: Generic buffer allocator can overflow size expansion
excluded_vulnerabilities.reason: `size_t total_size = size * 2; if (total_size < size)` catches unsigned wrap for multiplication by 2. The function is also not currently reachable from the benchmark entry paths, so treating it as a required vulnerability made the benchmark overfit to a questionable pattern.

excluded_vulnerabilities.former_title: Task validation uses mutable task payload pointer without synchronization
excluded_vulnerabilities.reason: The current public path validates the freshly parsed Task before queueing it to worker threads, and the benchmark does not provide a concrete concurrent writer for task->payload.command.command. Without that shared-object premise this is speculative.

excluded_vulnerabilities.former_title: Plugin dispatch and executor task path acquire lock_a/lock_b in opposite order
excluded_vulnerabilities.reason: _plugin_dispatch locks g_shared_resources.lock_b then lock_a, while _executor_execute_task locks g_exec_resources.lock_a then lock_b. These are different mutex objects, so the original lock-order deadlock claim is not concrete in the current fixture.
